literal: " After marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt with gold thread.
idiomatic: After he married the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt threaded with gold.

literal: Meeting Li Shu, he was quite ashamed and said, "These clothes of mine were all cut within the palace; now that I have seen you, my general, I cannot be without shame."
idiomatic: When he met Li Shu he was ashamed and said, "These clothes were all cut in the inner palace; now that I have seen you, my general, I cannot help feeling shame."

literal: When he occupied the summit of government, power embraced the pivots of state; ten thousand ends and threads—his spirit had no sluggish application.
idiomatic: Once he stood at the head of government and held the levers of power, ten thousand matters came before him and his mind never lagged.

literal: From Tianbao year 5 onward, when one man lost virtue, sustaining and rescue in truth had reliance in him.
idiomatic: From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when the emperor lost his virtue, the realm's stability and repair truly depended on him.

literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven came to the hall, the lords and ministers received investiture in obeisance; he issued names and sent forth orders, proclaiming edicts and registers.
idiomatic: Whenever the emperor appeared at court for investitures and edicts, Yang Yin proclaimed the orders and read out the imperial writs.

literal: Yin's diction was warm and eloquent, his bearing brilliant; the hundred officials watching and listening were all stirred and awed.
idiomatic: Yang Yin's diction was warm and fluent, his bearing brilliant; the officials who watched and listened were all stirred.

literal: From the time he occupied the high seat, his gate cut off private friendship.
idiomatic: From the time he rose to supreme power he shut his gate to private friendships.

literal: He held goods light and weight righteousness heavy; rewards before and after accumulated in the tens of thousands—he dispersed them among the nine clans; in his shelves and boxes there were only several thousand scrolls of books.
idiomatic: He valued righteousness over wealth; rewards that accumulated to vast sums he gave away among his clansmen, and in his cupboards he kept only several thousand books.

literal: Grand Mentor, Prince Longzhi of Pingyuan, was Yang Yin's neighbor; Yin once saw several rich Hu men outside his gate and told his attendants, "Fortunately there is no such thing before my gate.
idiomatic: Grand mentor Prince Longzhi of Pingyuan lived next to Yang Yin. Yin once saw several wealthy foreigners at Longzhi's gate and told his attendants, "Fortunately there is none of that at my gate.

literal: His nature was thorough, cautious and timid, always as if insufficient; whenever he heard a later command his expression changed mournfully.
idiomatic: His nature was thorough and cautious, always as if he fell short; whenever he heard a fresh order his face fell.

literal: When Wenxuan was critically ill, because the princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and kin and pressed near, he was deeply concerned about what would follow.
idiomatic: As Emperor Wenxuan sank toward death, he worried deeply about the aftermath, for the princes of Changshan and Changgung stood too close in kinship and power.

literal: Yin with Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, Palace Attendant Yan Zixian, and Yellow Gate Vice Director Zheng Zimo received the testament to assist government; they all, because the two princes' prestige was already heavy, had hearts of suspicion.
idiomatic: Yang Yin with left vice director Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, palace attendant Yan Zixian, and yellow gate vice director Zheng Zimo received the deathbed testament to govern as regents; because the two princes already carried such weight, all harbored suspicion.

literal: At first in Jinyang, because the departed lay in encoffining and the Son of Heaven was in mourning gloom, it was proposed that the prince of Changshan stay at the eastern lodge; whatever one wished to memorialize should first be consulted and decided.
idiomatic: At first in Jinyang, while the late emperor lay in state and the young emperor mourned in seclusion, the regents proposed that the prince of Changshan stay at the eastern lodge and that all memorials pass through him first.

literal: After twenty days it stopped.
idiomatic: This lasted twenty days and then ceased.

literal: They still wished the prince of Changshan to follow the coffin to Ye and leave the prince of Changgung to garrison Jinyang.
idiomatic: They next wished the prince of Changshan to accompany the coffin to Ye and the prince of Changgung to hold Jinyang.

literal: The ruling ministers again bred doubt and division; both princes again both followed and arrived at Ye.
idiomatic: The regents again grew divided and doubtful, and both princes followed on to Ye together.

literal: Zixian set up a plan wishing to place the grand empress dowager in the northern palace and return government to the empress dowager.
idiomatic: Zixian proposed housing the grand empress dowager in the northern palace so that power would rest with the empress dowager.

literal: Moreover, from Tianbao year 8 titles and rewards had been excessive; at this time Yin first memorialized himself to resign his opening-office enfeoffment as king, and all who had improperly received favor and glory were dismissed.
idiomatic: Moreover, since the eighth year of Tianbao enfeoffments and rewards had run wild; now Yin was first to memorial requesting release from his privy chamber and royal title, and all who had improperly gained rank were stripped.

literal: Hence those of the favorites who lost their posts all turned their hearts to the two uncles.
idiomatic: Hence the displaced favorites all threw their loyalty to the two princes.

literal: Gao Guiyan at first thought of the same virtue, later soon turned against them, reporting all traces of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes.
idiomatic: Gao Guiyan had first shared their purpose, but soon turned against them and told the two princes everything the regents had done out of suspicion.

literal: Kezhuhun Tianhe also often said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young lord has no principle by which to make himself secure.
idiomatic: Kezhuhun Tianhe also said repeatedly, "Unless the two princes are killed, the young emperor can never be secure.

literal: " Song Qindao addressed the emperor in person, saying the two uncles' prestige and power were already heavy and they should quickly be removed.
idiomatic: Song Qindao reported to the emperor in person that the two uncles' power was already too great and they should be removed at once.

literal: The emperor did not consent and said, "This may be jointly examined in detail with the director.
idiomatic: The emperor refused and said, "Take the matter up in full counsel with the director.

literal: " Yin and the rest discussed sending the two princes out as inspectors.
idiomatic: Yang Yin and the others debated posting the two princes to provincial inspectorates.

literal: Because the emperor was benevolent, fearing what they memorialized might not be accepted, they sent a sealed report to the empress dowager, setting forth safety and peril in full.
idiomatic: Fearing the benevolent emperor would not approve their memorial, they sent a private report to the empress dowager explaining the danger in full.

literal: There was a palace woman Li Changyi, wife of North Yuzhou Inspector Gao Zhongmi; because of Zhongmi's case she entered the palace; the empress dowager, because of Changyi's clan tie, was very intimate and fond.
idiomatic: A palace woman named Li Changyi, wife of North Yuzhou inspector Gao Zhongmi, had entered the palace because of her husband's case; the empress dowager, who was kin to Changyi, favored her greatly.

literal: The empress dowager showed her the report; Changyi secretly reported to the grand empress dowager.
idiomatic: The empress dowager showed her the report; Changyi secretly informed the grand empress dowager.

literal: Yin and the rest again discussed that the two princes must not both be sent out; they memorialized making the prince of Changgung Grand Marshal and inspector of Bing, the prince of Changshan Grand Preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: The regents then decided the two princes must not both leave the capital and memorialized appointing the prince of Changgung grand marshal and Bingzhou inspector, and the prince of Changshan grand preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing.

literal: When the two princes took office, at the Masters of Writing they convened the hundred officials in great assembly; Yin and the rest were all about to go together.
idiomatic: When the two princes were to take their offices the court planned a great assembly of officials at the Masters of Writing; Yang Yin and the others were all to attend.

literal: Zimo stopped them, saying, "The matter cannot be measured—one must not lightly strip off caution.
idiomatic: Zimo restrained them, saying, "The outcome cannot be foreseen; do not go unprepared.

literal: " Yin said, "We in utmost sincerity embody the state—how could there be principle in not attending when Changshan takes office? Why suddenly this worry?
idiomatic: Yang Yin said, "We serve the state in utter loyalty. How could we fail to attend when the prince of Changshan takes office? Why this sudden fear?

literal: " The prince of Changgung at dawn hid several tens of household slaves in the rear chamber of the recorder of the masters of writing; moreover he made understanding with several meritorious nobles at the seat.
idiomatic: The prince of Changgung hid dozens of household slaves in the recorder's rear chamber and confided in several honored nobles at the banquet.

literal: He also made a pact with the meritorious scions: when wine comes to Yin and the rest, each of us will urge a double cup; they are sure to decline.
idiomatic: He agreed with the meritorious young nobles: when wine reaches Yang Yin and the others, each of us urges a double cup—they are sure to decline.

literal: I once say 'Seize the wine,' twice 'Seize the wine,' thrice 'Why not seize?'—you lot seize at once.
idiomatic: At my first cry of 'Seize them!' and second 'Seize them!' and third 'Why not seize them?'—you seize them at once.

literal: When the banquet came it was as planned.
idiomatic: At the banquet all went as planned.

literal: Yin shouted, "Princes, you plot rebellion—you wish to kill the loyal and good?
idiomatic: Yang Yin cried out, "You princes plot treason—do you mean to kill loyal men?

literal: Honor the Son of Heaven, reduce the feudal lords—we give our red hearts to serve the state; we ought not come to this.
idiomatic: We honor the emperor, curtail the princes, and give our loyal hearts to the state—we should not come to this!

literal: " The prince of Changshan wished to ease matters; the prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be.
idiomatic: The prince of Changshan wished to relent; the prince of Changgung said, "No.

literal: " Thereupon Yin and Tianhe and Qindao were all struck and beaten in disorder with fists and staves; heads and faces streamed blood; ten men each held them.
idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were beaten with fists and clubs until blood ran from their heads and faces; ten men held each of them.

literal: They sent Xue Guyan and Kang Mai to seize Zimo at the Bureau of Imperial Pharmacy.
idiomatic: They sent Xue Guyan and Kang Mai to seize Zimo at the imperial pharmacy bureau.

literal: Zimo said, "By not using the wise man's words we have come to this—is it not fate!
idiomatic: Zimo said, "By not heeding the wise man's counsel we have come to this—is it not fate?"

literal: The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in hustling Yin and the rest in a rush through Cloud Dragon Gate.
idiomatic: The two princes led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in hustling Yang Yin and the others through Cloud Dragon Gate.

literal: They saw Commander Chilü Sao, summoned him; he would not advance; they had horsemen kill him.
idiomatic: They saw commander Chilü Sao, summoned him, and when he would not advance they had horsemen cut him down.

literal: Acting Three Excellencies Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan instructed him, and only then could they enter.
idiomatic: Cheng Xiuning, who held privy chamber rank, blocked the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and they entered.

literal: They sent Yin and the rest before the emperor.
idiomatic: They brought Yang Yin and the others before the emperor.

literal: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside Vermilion Flower Gate.
idiomatic: The prince of Changgung and Guiyan waited outside Vermilion Flower Gate.

literal: The grand empress dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the empress dowager and the emperor stood at the side.
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager presided in Zhaoyang Hall; the empress dowager and the emperor stood at her side.

literal: The prince of Changshan knocked his head with brick and advanced, saying, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bone and flesh joined.
idiomatic: The prince of Changshan knocked his head on the brick floor and said, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bound in the same flesh.

literal: Yang Zunyan and the rest wished to monopolize court power; authority and blessing were theirs alone; from kings and dukes down all stood on tiptoe and held their breath.
idiomatic: Yang Zunyan and his circle meant to monopolize court power and keep bounty in their own hands; from kings and dukes down everyone stood in dread.

literal: They were lip and teeth to each other and made the steps of disorder; if not plotted against early, they would surely harm the altars of state.
idiomatic: They were mouth and gum to one another and piled step on step toward chaos; unless checked early they would ruin the altars of state.

literal: Your servant and Zhan and the rest took state affairs as weighty; Heba Ren, Hulu Jin and the rest cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; together we seized Zunyan and the rest and led them into the palace; we did not yet dare execution and punishment; the fault of arrogating authority deserves ten thousand deaths.
idiomatic: Your servant and Zhan took the weight of state upon ourselves; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Gao Huan's foundation; we seized Zunyan and his fellows and brought them into the palace. We have not yet executed them; for our presumption we deserve ten thousand deaths.

literal: " The emperor was silent; Liu Taozhi of the garrison-general and his kind guarded the steps, striking blades and looking up; the emperor would not glance at them; the grand empress dowager ordered them to lay aside weapons; they would not.
idiomatic: The emperor said nothing. Garrison-general Liu Taozhi and his guards stood on the stairs, hands on their blades, looking up at him; the emperor would not meet their eyes. The grand empress dowager ordered them to stand down; they refused.

literal: She again said in a harsh voice, "Slaves—your heads fall this instant.
idiomatic: She shouted again, "Slaves—off with your heads this instant!

literal: " Then they withdrew.
idiomatic: Then they withdrew.

literal: She then asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out.
idiomatic: She asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already gone.

literal: The grand empress dowager said mournfully, "What could Master Yang do—would it not have been better to keep him!
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager said in grief, "What harm could Master Yang have done—was it not better to keep him!

literal: " She then reproached the emperor: "These men harbored rebellion, wished to kill my two sons, next would reach me—why did you indulge them?
idiomatic: She reproached the emperor: "These men plotted rebellion; they meant to kill my two sons and next would reach me—why did you indulge them?

literal: " The emperor still could not speak.
idiomatic: The emperor still could not speak.

literal: The grand empress dowager was angry and grieved; kings and dukes all wept.
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager was torn between anger and grief; the princes and dukes wept.

literal: The grand empress dowager said, "How can you let us mother and son be measured out by an old Han crone!
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager said, "How can you let us mother and son be ruled by an old Han woman!

literal: " The empress dowager bowed in apology.
idiomatic: The empress dowager bowed in apology.

literal: The prince of Changshan knocked his head without cease.
idiomatic: The prince of Changshan kept knocking his head on the floor.

literal: The grand empress dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort and soothe your uncle?
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle?

literal: The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven also dares not spare them for his uncle's sake—how much less spare these Han fellows?
idiomatic: The emperor then said, "Even the Son of Heaven dares not withhold them from his uncle—how much less these Han fellows?

literal: I only wish to beg my son's life; your son will leave the hall—this lot is left to uncle's disposal.
idiomatic: I beg only for my son's life; your son will leave the hall—dispose of this lot as you will.

literal: " Thereupon all were beheaded.
idiomatic: Thereupon all were beheaded.

literal: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in drafting an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.
idiomatic: The prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in an edict, first tore out his tongue and cut off his hands.

literal: The grand empress dowager attended Yin's mourning and wept, saying, "Master Yang was loyal yet received punishment.
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager attended Yang Yin's mourning and wept, "Master Yang was loyal yet was punished.

literal: " She used imperial gold to make one eye, personally placed it within, and said, "To show my mind.
idiomatic: She had an eye made of imperial gold and placed it in the coffin herself, saying, "This shows my heart.

literal: " The prince of Changshan also regretted killing him.
idiomatic: The prince of Changshan also regretted the killing.

literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said, "White sheep—head and tail bald; the ram's turn—horns grow on the head.
idiomatic: Earlier a children's rhyme had run, "The white sheep's head and tail are bare; the year of the ram brings horns on its brow.

literal: It also said, "Sheep, sheep eat wild grass; if you don't eat wild grass, keep far from my road; if you don't keep far, I'll beat your brains.
idiomatic: Another ran, "Sheep, sheep, graze the wild grass; leave the grass and you leave my road; stay near and I'll crack your skull.

literal: It also said, "Auntie brings calamity; the Daoist nun's brother-in-law dies.
idiomatic: Another said, "Auntie brings ruin; the tonsured princess's husbands die.

literal: Sheep was Yin; 'horn' written was using a knife; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Yin's Zixian and Tianhe were both the emperor's brothers-in-law.
idiomatic: Sheep stood for Yin; the character for 'horn' splits into 'use' and 'knife'; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Zixian and Tianhe, both sons-in-law of the house, were tied to the rhyme.

literal: Thereupon by the Son of Heaven's command an edict was issued condemning their crimes; guilt stopped at one person; households were not questioned.
idiomatic: Thereupon an edict in the emperor's name condemned them, limiting guilt to the men themselves and exempting their households.

literal: Soon registers were again made of five families; Wang Xi firmly remonstrated; thereupon one branch of each was confiscated; infant children and brothers were all struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: Before long registers were drawn up against five families; Wang Xi protested firmly; in the end one branch of each house was confiscated and brothers and children were struck from the rolls.

literal: When Zunyan died, Secretariat Director Zhao Yanshen was still used to replace him in overseeing critical affairs.
idiomatic: After Zunyan's death, secretariat director Zhao Yanshen was put in charge of state affairs in his place.

literal: Palace Reception Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi said privately to someone, "About to cross a thousand li, yet killing the qilin and driving the lame donkey—how deeply pitiable.
idiomatic: Palace reception vice director Yang Xiuzhi said privately, "One is about to cross a thousand li, yet kills the qilin and drives a lame donkey—how pitiful.

literal: Yin's compositions in poetry, rhapsodies, memorials, and legal briefs were very many; after execution they were scattered and lost; what his disciples gathered amounted to more than ten thousand words.
idiomatic: Yang Yin left many poems, fu, memorials, and pleading documents; after his execution most were lost, but his disciples gathered more than ten thousand words of what survived.

literal: Kezhuhun Tianhe was Daoyuan's youngest brother.
idiomatic: Kezhuhun Tianhe was the youngest brother of Daoyuan.

literal: Because Daoyuan had no weight of merit, he married the princess of Dongping.
idiomatic: Because his clan had little merit he was married to the princess of Dongping.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to garrison-general grand general and privy chamber.
idiomatic: He rose through posts to garrison-general, grand general, and privy chamber.

literal: When the prince of Jinan took the throne he was given special advance, changed to Duke of Boling, and was killed together with Yang Yin.
idiomatic: When the prince of Jinan took the throne he was made special advance and duke of Boling, and was killed together with Yang Yin.

literal: Song Qindao was a man of Guangping, grandson of Wei Minister of Personnel Bian.
idiomatic: Song Qindao was from Guangping, grandson of Wei minister of personnel Song Bian.

literal: At first he was chief clerk to the grand general, in charge of records.
idiomatic: He began as chief clerk to the grand general, keeping the records.

literal: Later he was yellow gate vice director.
idiomatic: Later he became yellow gate vice director.

literal: He was also ordered to the eastern palace to teach the heir apparent administrative matters.
idiomatic: He was also assigned to the eastern palace to instruct the crown prince in affairs of state.

literal: At the time Zheng Zimo was known for literary accomplishment and also enjoyed intimate favor.
idiomatic: At that time Zheng Zimo was known for his learning and shared intimate favor at court.

literal: Qindao by origin was a clerk versed in statutes, not very familiar with past and present; whenever there was a doubtful matter he always inquired of Zimo.
idiomatic: Qindao was by training a legal clerk, not deeply versed in history; whenever he was unsure he asked Zimo.

literal: The two men were favored by both palaces; even princes and eminent ministers did not fail to respect and fear them.
idiomatic: Both were favorites of the two palaces; even princes and great ministers feared them.

literal: Qindao was again promoted to director of the secretariat library.
idiomatic: Qindao was later promoted to director of the secretariat library.

literal: He was executed together with Yang Yin; posthumously granted Minister of Personnel and inspector of Zhao.
idiomatic: He was executed with Yang Yin and posthumously made minister of personnel and inspector of Zhao.

literal: Zheng Yi, style Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Zheng Yi, style Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng.

literal: High ancestor Ju held Pengcheng for Wei and moved from Xingyang thither.
idiomatic: His distant ancestor Ju held Pengcheng for Wei and moved there from Xingyang.

literal: Yi was clever and quick, and had broadly touched literary meaning.
idiomatic: Yi was clever and well read in the literary tradition.

literal: At first he was eastern-pavilion libationer to the prince of Taiyuan, and was especially friendly with Song Qindao; Qindao always treated him as master.
idiomatic: He first served as eastern-pavilion libationer to the prince of Taiyuan and was especially close to Song Qindao, who treated him as his teacher.

literal: Yang Yin at first looked down on Song and Zheng and did not extend ceremony to them.
idiomatic: Yang Yin at first despised Song and Zheng and did not treat them with courtesy.

literal: Before long he bound himself to the ruler and participated in the deathbed testament.
idiomatic: Before long Zheng Yi bound himself to the ruler and joined the regency.

literal: Qindao renewed his old intimacy with Jinan and mutual introduction; nothing was left unsaid.
idiomatic: Qindao renewed his old closeness with the prince of Jinan; they drew each other on and held nothing back.

literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was appointed attendant cavalier in regular attendance.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianming Zheng Yi was made attendant cavalier in regular attendance.
